module

public import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Prod
public import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Image
public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Defs

@[expose] public section

/-!
# Restricted sumsets

This file defines the restricted sumset $S \hat{+} S$ for a finite set $S$.
-/

namespace Finset

variable {α : Type*} [Add α] [DecidableEq α]

/--
The restricted sumset of a set $S$, denoted $S \hat{+} S$, is the set
$\lbrace s_1 + s_2 : s_1, s_2 \in S, s_1 \neq s_2 \rbrace$.
-/
def restrictedSumset (S : Finset α) : Finset α :=
  S.offDiag.image (fun p => p.1 + p.2)

end Finset

reformulations.difference: Sanders defines M(A) as a maximum over sum-avoiding subsets; Lean uses Finset.sup over a filtered powerset.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The powerset enumerates exactly the subsets of A, and the filter expresses precisely the required disjointness. The candidate family always contains the empty set, so the finite supremum is an attained maximum, including when A is empty. Proved in Lean, for every real r, that r ≤ M(A) iff there exists S ⊆ A with Disjoint S.restrictedSumset A and r ≤ S.card.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses natural-number subtraction in min (2 * A.card - 3) p and permits A = ∅, whereas ANR96 Theorem 1.3 uses the signed bound and assumes A is nonempty.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For cardinality at least two, subtraction is untruncated and the bounds coincide. For cardinality zero or one, the signed lower bound is negative and the truncated bound is zero; both inequalities hold automatically. Proved the equivalence in Lean between the all-finsets natural-number statement and the nonempty-finsets integer-valued statement, for every p.

review.notes: The sole declaration, Finset.restrictedSumset, matches the standard notion exactly. A Lean proof establishes x ∈ S.restrictedSumset iff ∃ a ∈ S, ∃ b ∈ S, a ≠ b ∧ a + b = x. The ordered-pair image deduplicates sums correctly; it also retains values having both diagonal and off-diagonal representations. No existing Mathlib duplicate or incompatible use was found. Experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and use_sites.lean compile successfully and cover empty sets/types, singletons, subsingleton structures, sum collisions, noncommutative addition, and ZMod 0, 1, 2, 3. All three use-site files use the intended restricted-sum semantics. Erdős pages 476 and 484 and the original 1994 DOI were blocked by Cloudflare; the mathematical statement of 476 was independently verified against ANR96 Theorem 1.3. The target file remains identical to its committed version.
